chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ibrahim ibn Hashim and al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi from al-Husayn ibn Sayf from his brother Ali from his father from 'Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Jibrail (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Muhammad, good fortune for whoever from your Ummah says: La ilaha illallah, He is alone, He is alone, He is alone.'

key_terms.طُوبَی: Tooba, a tree in Paradise or a state of good fortune
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: La ilaha illallah, the declaration of monotheism

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting 'La ilaha illallah Wahdahu' three times?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* highlights the spiritual merit of emphasizing the absolute oneness of God (*Wahdahu*) through tripling, linking it to 'Tooba,' a specific tree or station in Paradise. In Shia tradition, this underscores the centrality of *Tawhid* not just as a theological tenet but as a devotional act that secures divine favor and eternal reward for the faithful.
